rules.title: Evaluation and escalation

escalationBody.self: Self-care: follow the guide. No one needs to be notified.
escalationBody.crew: Crew: the onboard medical officer was notified because the value keeps falling out of range.
escalationBody.flightSurgeon: Flight surgeon: the crew was notified and the report is on its way to Earth (arrives after the link delay).

rules.remeasure: Measure again in {{min}} min at rest to confirm.

kinds.news2: Rule: NEWS2 score (0 normal · 1–2 caution · 3 critical).
kinds.aha: Rule: AHA blood pressure categories + systolic ≤ 90 (NEWS2).
kinds.baseline: Rule: comparison with YOUR personal baseline (not a clinical threshold; the flight surgeon can adjust the margin).
kinds.none: No validated onboard rule: stored and sent for expert review.
kinds.sex: Rule: clinical limit that differs for men and women.

reasons.news2Low: Slightly out of range per NEWS2.
reasons.news2High: Far out of range per NEWS2.
reasons.bpCrisis: Blood pressure in hypertensive crisis range (AHA).
reasons.noBaseline: No personal baseline yet (3 readings needed).
reasons.noRule: Logged for review: no validated onboard rule.
reasons.gripLow: Strength below the cut-off for your sex (EWGSOP2).
reasons.calciumHigh: Urinary calcium above the limit for your sex.
reasons.noSex: Your sex is missing from your record, so it cannot be evaluated.

register.title: Log measurement
register.subtitle: Manually or with a photo of the device
register.permissionBody: Allow camera or photo access in the phone settings.
register.invalid: Check the value: it must be between {{min}} and {{max}} (diastolic lower than systolic).
register.photoBody: Take a photo of the measuring device's screen. It is stored on the device as evidence so the flight surgeon can verify the reading. Offline there is no automatic reading: type the number you see below.

achievements.title: Achievements
achievements.subtitle: Completing is rewarded, never the result
achievements.fairPlay: An out-of-range value earns the same as a normal one: what matters is measuring and reporting honestly.

camera.title: Evidence
camera.body: Log a reading with a photo.

allTests.title: Sharp mind
allTests.body: All 4 tests on the same day.

how: Rest for 5 minutes seated or strapped into your sleeping bag, without talking.
Put the pulse oximeter on your index finger (or use the wristband) and keep your hand still at heart level.
Wait at least 30 seconds for the value to settle.
Log the value. If you just exercised, wait 15 minutes before measuring.
heartRate.meaning: Beats per minute at rest. In microgravity fluids shift toward the head and the heart works differently; stress, fever or dehydration also raise it. Evaluated with the NEWS2 table: 51–90 is normal.

actions.normal: Keep your routine and the scheduled measurement.
actions.caution: Rest, hydrate and measure again in 15 min. If it repeats out of range, the medical officer is notified.
actions.critical: Stop the activity, rest and notify the crew now. Escalated to the flight surgeon.
actions.unevaluated: Log the value; it will be reviewed later.

how: Rest for 5 minutes with your back supported and feet secured.
Place the cuff on the bare arm, 2–3 cm above the elbow, at heart level.
Do not talk or move during the measurement.
Take two readings 1 minute apart and log the second.
bloodPressure.meaning: Systolic / diastolic in mmHg. In flight, fluid shifts and cardiovascular deconditioning change it. Normal (AHA): below 120/80. Elevated: 120–129. High: from 130/80. Crisis: above 180/120. A systolic of 90 or less is also critical (NEWS2).

actions.normal: No action. Repeat per the mission schedule.
actions.caution: Repeat in 15 min at rest. Cut salt and caffeine that day. If it persists, the crew is notified.
actions.critical: Rest immediately and notify the crew. If there is chest pain, severe dizziness or blurred vision, activate triage.
actions.unevaluated: Log the value; it will be reviewed later.

how: Warm your hands if they are cold.
Place the pulse oximeter on a finger without nail polish and keep your hand still.
Wait for a stable pulse wave (about 30 s).
Log the value.
spo2.meaning: Percentage of oxygen in the blood. Depends on the cabin atmosphere (CO₂, pressure) and the lungs. NEWS2: 96% or more is normal; 92–95% caution; 91% or less critical.

actions.caution: Breathe deeply, check the module's CO₂ sensors and measure again. If it persists, notify the crew.
actions.critical: Notify the crew now and check the module atmosphere. Use oxygen per the onboard procedure.
actions.unevaluated: Log the value; it will be reviewed later.

how: Put on the respiratory band or ask a crewmate to watch your chest.
Breathe normally, without trying to control the rhythm.
Count breaths for a full 60 seconds.
Log the number.
respRate.meaning: Breaths per minute. Rises with fever, high CO₂, anxiety or pain. NEWS2: 12–20 is normal.

actions.caution: Rest and measure again in 15 min. Check the module CO₂.
actions.critical: Notify the crew. More than 25 or fewer than 9 per minute needs immediate attention.
actions.unevaluated: Log the value; it will be reviewed later.

how: Take the reaction test somewhere quiet, always with the same tablet.
Hold the device firmly and use the same finger every time.
Tap as soon as the stimulus appears, without anticipating.
The result is saved automatically.
reactionTime.meaning: Measures your alertness. Sleep loss, fatigue and stress slow it down. It is compared with YOUR baseline (there is no universal 'normal' value): more than 15% worse than your average is caution.

actions.normal: You are within your usual range.
actions.caution: Prioritize rest. Before a critical task repeat the test; if fitness is not confirmed, talk to the commander.
actions.unevaluated: You need 3 tests to build your baseline.

how: Follow the onboard tonometer procedure with help from the medical officer.
Apply the anesthetic drop if the device requires it.
Measure each eye separately and log the higher value.
You can attach a photo of the tonometer screen.
eyePressure.meaning: Pressure inside the eye in mmHg. On long flights spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome (SANS) can appear. American Academy of Ophthalmology reference: 10–21 mmHg.

actions.caution: Take the visual clarity test and note any vision changes. The flight surgeon will review the trend.
actions.unevaluated: Log the value; it will be reviewed later.

how: Collect 24-hour urine with the onboard kit.
Process the sample following the analyzer procedure.
Log the value in mg/day and attach a photo of the result.
urinaryCalcium.meaning: In microgravity bones lose calcium, which is excreted in urine (raising the risk of kidney stones). It is considered high above 275 mg/day in men and 250 mg/day in women.

actions.normal: Keep up resistance exercise and your usual hydration.
actions.caution: Drink more water, review your resistance exercise and tell the medical officer. The flight surgeon will review the trend.
actions.unevaluated: Log the value; it will be reviewed later.

how: Hold the dynamometer with your arm against your body and elbow at 90°.
Squeeze as hard as you can for 3 seconds.
Do 3 attempts with your dominant hand and log the best.
gripStrength.meaning: Grip strength in kg, a proxy for muscle mass. Without gravity muscles atrophy unless trained. It is considered low below 27 kg in men and 16 kg in women; in addition, a drop of more than 10% from your baseline is caution.

actions.caution: Review your resistance exercise (ARED) compliance with the crew.
actions.unevaluated: You need 3 readings to build your baseline.

how: Do not eat or drink anything hot or cold 15 minutes before.
Place the thermometer according to its type (forehead, ear or oral).
Wait for the device signal and log the value.
bodyTemperature.meaning: Body temperature in °C. Fever may indicate an infection; the immune system behaves differently in space. NEWS2: 36.1–38.0 °C is normal.

actions.caution: Hydrate, rest and measure again in 1 h. Note symptoms in your check-in.
actions.critical: Notify the crew and isolate if the protocol says so. Escalated to the flight surgeon.
actions.unevaluated: Log the value; it will be reviewed later.

measureSession.title: Log measurement
measureSession.subtitle: Today's pending measurements
measureSession.mustComplete: The session ends when all are done. If you leave, it is saved and you resume where you left off.
measureSession.howTitle: How do you want to do them?
measureSession.guidedHint: We take you from one to the next in the recommended order (blood pressure first, at rest).
measureSession.freeHint: You pick the order from the list; all must still be completed.
measureSession.completeBody: All of today's measurements were logged and evaluated.

measureSession.nothingBody: You already logged everything due today.

sexRange.title: Normal range for you
sexRange.same: The clinical source uses the same range for men and women.

explain.heartRate: Range between the 5th and 95th percentiles of healthy adults at rest. On average, women have a higher pulse than men (74 vs 71 bpm from age 20). Alerts still follow the NEWS2 clinical rule, which is the same for both sexes.
explain.urinaryCalcium: Above this value it is considered hypercalciuria. The limit is lower for women.
explain.gripStrength: Below this value grip strength is considered low (sarcopenia cut-off). It is also compared with your own baseline.
